title: OpenAI Staff Warned Management of Security Flaws Before ChatGPT Release
summary:
Employees at the AI startup flagged vulnerabilities in internal security measures to executives and the board years before the late 2022 release of its hallmark chatbot, five people familiar with the matter told Reuters. Staff warned that the company's use of a single 'monorepo' for most of its code allowed anyone with access to view sensitive details of projects outside their scope of work. Some employees concluded that the pressure to keep pace with competitors like Google and Anthropic took priority over addressing these gaps.

OpenAI stated that its most sensitive work and model weights are stored outside the monorepo. To address existing vulnerabilities, the company says it recently assigned 25% of its product engineers to identify and fix security flaws.

selectedTweets.text:
The timeline here is troubling.

Reuters reports that employees took security concerns to OpenAI’s leadership and board before ChatGPT launched. Some left those discussions believing competition was taking priority.

OpenAI says it recently devoted 25% of its product engineers to finding and fixing vulnerabilities.

That’s a serious commitment. I’d want to see it survive the next release deadline. Security only works if it remains a priority when the pressure to move faster returns.
